name: Christine Geertsema
testimonial:
Dear Mrs Bates.

I honestly do not how to construct this letter. Where do you begin thanking someone who changed your life and help turn your dreams into a reality?

When I first met you, I was this scared, insecure first year student, who was too afraid to believe in herself. However, despite that, I knew I needed to reach out, because I had to fight for my dream. I was not strong enough to fight on my own and lucky for me you had the intuition to see that.

I first consulted you, when I felt like I was underperforming in Chemistry, a subject that has always been difficult for me, and as a result I did not like it too much. You guided me, by using your own personal time, and went through my past papers with me question by question. Not only did I understand the work better, but I also had a better understanding of how to answer questions and interpret them, which is one of the most important skills a teacher can teach a student. Not spoon-feeding me but altering the way I think about chemistry. After our first session, my marks increased astronomically, jumping from a 72% to an 89%. As you know from experience, this is almost unheard of, especially for a first-year student and with a subject like Chemistry. As you know it only increased from there and I scored close to 100% in my written exam.

I wanted to thank you for the numerous times you patiently explained concepts over and over and over to me (again, in your personal time). I want you to know that you changed my life, and no amount of gratitude will ever suffice. I can proudly say that I will be embarking on my journey to become a doctor and you have played an enormous role in making that happen.

The world needs more teachers like you, Mrs Bates. Teachers who care enough to see a kid with a dream and not just another student that needs to pass.

Thank you for believing in me, even when I did not believe in myself. I will forever be grateful.

Best of luck with your future and I know that you are going to change many more students' lives.

Kindest regards
